pages.text: All night, snow piled up to the door. The cabin was buried in it.
Nils wanted to clear a path to the well. They needed a path to fetch water; the water tub was empty.
Nils shoveled. Scoop, toss! Scoop, toss! Snow piled beside the path.
The path barely reached the steps. The well was still far away.
His arms ached. He threw down the shovel and flopped into the snow. "Too much snow. I can't."
Snow crept under his back. His neck was damp. Still, he didn't want to get up.
Evening came. Time for soup, but the water tub was empty. No path to the well.
Grandpa shoveled ten times, then straightened and rested once. "Resting is part of doing it too."
Nils shoveled ten times and rested once. A few rounds of that, and the path reached the well!
Grandpa drew water. Holding the tub, Nils looked back at the snowy path. It ran all the way to the well.
